Subject: Mutual Action Plan: acceptance criteria, exit gates, and test runway

Hi Sarah —

As discussed in yesterday's demo, I've attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP_v1.xlsx) that lays out milestones, owners, and proposed acceptance tests for the evaluation. The goal here is to make the path to a decision transparent and measurable so we can avoid surprises during the trial.

Quick summary of proposed success criteria (high level):
- Accuracy/concordance: >= 92% on the annotated set for our top-3 intents
- Latency: 95th-percentile < 350ms for single-shot generation under typical load
- Stability: zero model restarts during 48-hour stress window
- Data handling: KV/cache expiration and PII redaction verified in runbook tests

Exit gates (examples):
1) Failfast: Any data exfiltration gap or missing audit log within scope -> stop and remediate
2) Quality: concordance below threshold across two consecutive runs -> rollback to baseline model
3) Ops: sustained 95th-latency > 500ms under real traffic -> performance remediation required

Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx (milestones + acceptance tests) and SLA_draft_redlines.docx (rough procurement starting point).

Can you confirm if these acceptance metrics align with your internal bar? Also, what procurement evidence do you need to start an SOW? Happy to iterate quickly.

Thanks,

Marissa / Karthik — adding the concrete acceptance-test checklist we'll run once Mediq's edge cases are added. I'm dropping the full test script below and will attach a runnable harness to MAP_v2.

Acceptance test checklist (run order):
1) Integration smoke (owner: CS) — API auth, prefix/caching enabled, sample generation success (3 prompts)
2) Data handling verification (owner: Security/CS) — ingest de-identified payloads, confirm redaction and no PII in logs
3) Concordance validation (owner: Solutions) — 2-pass scoring against annotated set, threshold >= 92%
4) Latency sweep (owner: Infra) — ramp to baseline throughput, record p50/p95/p99; target p95 < 350ms
5) Stability run (owner: CS) — 48h stress with synthetic traffic and KV-cache pressure; zero restarts
6) Audit & logging check (owner: Security) — confirm retrieval of all request/response traces and KMS key usage logs

Acceptance criteria will be recorded in the MAP as pass/fail with evidence links (screenshots, logs, test harness outputs). If any gate fails twice after remediation, we trigger the "stop and fix" protocol documented in the MAP.

I'll deliver the harness and a short runbook snippet as attachments to the MAP_v2 package.

—Ben
